column1: arrival|Hale is in the research room. The door is open; he seems to be searching his desk.|Should I go in now?|Yes. He has cleared the end of the desk nearest the door for you.|I will go and say hello.|You can return when you are ready.|The doorway is clear. Hale looks up as you enter.

hale_phone|There you are. This is your Trainer Phone. I saved Mira and Mara's numbers. Mine... let me check that again.|Who should I contact first?|Mira looks after Pokémon nearby. Call me if you need help with the journey. Mara wants to meet you at the training grounds.|I will take the phone. Thank you, Professor.|All right. I will keep it here until you want to begin.|Here you go. Mira is nearby; let her check your party before you head out.

mira_visit|Hello. Hale said you are starting your journey. Would you like me to check your Pokémon?|Do they have to be injured before I visit?|No. I can check a healthy party too. If you are battling, though, we need to wait until the battle ends.|Please check my party, Mira.|That is fine. Come back whenever they need care.|Bring them over. I will check each one.

ren_supplies|Need Poké Balls or medicine? Have a look at the prices first. You do not have to buy today.|Will skipping the shop stop me from meeting Mara?|No. Mara does not need a receipt from me to accept a challenge. I sell travel supplies; that is all.|Let me browse the shop.|All right. I am here if you need supplies later.|Take your time. The price is shown before you buy anything.

lan_errand|Have you met Hale? He left his lunch at my house again. Could you take some apples over to him?|How many apples should I bring?|Three will do. Hand them to him, please, or they will disappear behind his books.|I will bring him three apples.|When you have time, then. I will find another way to remind him too.|Thank you. Please give them to Hale himself.

hale_lunch|Lan's apples? I thought I had only been reading for a little while. Thank you for bringing them.|Where should I meet Mara next?|At the training grounds. She asked whether you had arrived. Bring a party you know well; it does not have to be large.|Here are the three apples Lan sent.|Come back if you do not have enough yet. I will eat what is here first.|Good, all three. I will put the books down and eat before you leave.

mara_intro|You are the trainer Hale mentioned? I am Mara. I would like a battle once you have prepared your party.|What do you want to see in this battle?|How you choose a move when your first plan stops working. And I want to win. It is no more complicated than that.|I will prepare my party, then challenge you.|I train here. If you do not want to battle yet, say so.|All right. Come back when your party is ready.

mara_first|Is your party ready? Mine is. Do you want to start?|Can we try again if I lose?|Yes. Heal your party and return. A loss does not cancel our appointment.|Ready. Let us begin.|All right. Do not accept while your party still needs care.|Then let us see what each party can do.

field_fault|The training log has two finish times, one second apart. The video shows one battle.|Could this just be a clock error?|An old account confirmed the result before the battle ended. That account predates the grounds. Keep the original record for comparison.|I will keep this record and take it to Hale.|You can examine the record again later.|The original record is preserved for Hale to examine.

hale_fault|This confirmation code... I recognize its structure. It does not tell us who sent it. Orin has an independent copy of the old records.|Why should I meet Orin?|He keeps records in the second town. Comparing the copies can locate the change. Do not edit yours, even if someone messages you to do it.|I will take the original to Orin.|Keep the original safe. There is no need to rush.|Good. Take this copy intact; I will keep the one here.

unknown_first|Someone asked me to pass this on. I asked their name; they only said, 'Hale will understand.'|What was the message?|Do not edit the log. Keep the original. Last time they changed the winner's name too. The phone only shows three question marks. Show Mara as well.|I will show Mara the message.|You do not have to reply to that person immediately.|Good. Let Mara see exactly what they sent.

mara_aftermath|I read it. They know about the log, but that is not enough to trust them. I will keep my own copy.|What will you do while I visit Orin?|Compare the grounds' record. If mine changes while you are away, we will know. Let us keep each other updated by phone.|I will visit Orin and keep you updated.|Prepare first. I will not send this copy to a stranger.|Agreed. Call if something changes; I will do the same.

orin_arrival|Looking for Orin? He is asking about a tournament results book taken from the library.|Where can I check the lending record?|A copy is on the reading table. Check the date and who borrowed it before speaking with him.|I will check the list on the reading table.|I will leave the copy there for later.|The copy is on the table. Start with the date.

orin_records|Seven books were borrowed on one day by a League department. In the award photo, a line of names was cropped out.|Does this signature match the training record?|Their confirmation signatures have the same structure. That can be compared. We still do not know whose name was removed.|I will show the signature to Orin.|The copy remains here if you want to check it again.|You retain the signature and lending date for comparison.

orin_challenge|I examined your record. Before we discuss conclusions, I want to see how you handle a situation that keeps changing.|You want to use a battle as an example?|Yes. My party uses status conditions and switches. Watch the turns that do not cause damage too. We will discuss the record afterward.|I agree. Please begin the battle.|Prepare your party first. We can wait.|Then observe what changes, including between attacks.

orin_summary|Two independent archives show the same edit, despite different saving schedules. Whoever changed them knew which copies would be compared.|Did Hale know those copies had been changed?|Hale kept the records private to stop the system being reused. I objected, but also kept my copy private. Ask both of us for evidence. Rook holds an old transport access card.|I will find Rook and examine the access card.|You can review our comparisons before leaving.|Take the comparison with you. Ask Rook where that card has been used.

rook_contact|I delivered crates to Rook with the same black-card mark. He called them ordinary goods, but received them after the warehouse closed.|Is there paperwork that can verify his account?|The warehouse has an invoice from one shipment. Read it first. Rook gives better answers when he knows you have seen the paperwork.|I will examine the warehouse invoice.|The invoice is staying here. You can return later.|I will point out which invoice belongs to that shipment.

black_invoice|The Black Card originally allowed emergency Warden transport. This shipment was opened after closing, under the name of someone not on duty.|Where was it delivered?|A transport company's warehouse in the sixth town. The receiving mark is linked to Rocket. Rook needs to explain why his card was used there.|I will ask Rook about this invoice.|Compare the paperwork further before drawing a conclusion.|Keep the destination and receiving mark together.

rook_battle|Read the invoice? I have the card. Before I hand it over, show me you can keep it when someone wants it back.|Why do I need to battle for it?|Warehouse staff will not step aside for paperwork alone. I want to know you can get your party out. Win, and I give you the card and what I know.|I accept. Let us begin.|The card stays with me. No need to pretend you are ready.|All right. Win this, and I keep my end of the agreement.

rook_warning|That invoice is from last week. Selene says the warehouse closed long ago. Someone is leaving part of the story out.|Was Iris involved in the shipment?|She once asked me to take a copy of some records outside. I kept the receipt. Check the vehicle with Selene before blaming Iris for this.|I will compare the shipment with Selene.|Read the receipt first. I do not need an immediate verdict.|Take the receipt. Compare what each of us actually claims.

selene_local|A League truck came through at night. The roadside leaves were burnt the next morning. Selene said it carried medicine, so I kept the gate log.|Who authorized its entry?|Selene signed. But the gate paper records the medicine shipment, not what the truck actually carried. Check the delivery order too.|I will check the log at the guard post.|The log is still there. I have not given it away.|Look at the delivery order alongside the gate log.

selene_log|Selene's paper lists medicine. The delivery order was changed to record-storage equipment, confirmed by the League office.|So her signature does not prove she changed the cargo?|Correct. It proves she approved the original medicine shipment. Rook may be right about the truck while Selene is right about the cargo she was told about.|I will ask Selene about the changed order.|Keep both papers so the truck and its cargo do not get confused.|You retain both versions of the order.

selene_battle|You brought both papers. Good. I will trace the edit, but first I need to know you can protect the originals.|You still do not trust me?|I trust that you checked. At the warehouse they will pressure you to give up what you are carrying. This battle shows me how you handle pressure.|Then let us battle.|Needing time to prepare does not mean refusing the investigation.|All right. Keep your attention on the battle; we can examine the order afterward.

selene_aftermath|I will send the log to Mara. Wardens manage emergency warehouse access. If the card was copied, they need to know.|What should I take to the Warden?|The changed order and card mark. They show access was misused, not that every Warden was involved.|I will bring the evidence to the Warden station.|I will keep a copy so your journey cannot lose our only lead.|Take those two records. I will send my copy to Mara.

warden_ranger|Pokémon avoid this road when the truck comes, but not when people walk by. I want to check its cargo.|Does the station record when the truck arrives?|Yes, on the duty board. Read the dates, then report them. I need a safe rescue route, not another rumor about a truck.|I will compare the duty board.|I marked those days. You can read them later.|Compare the dates before reporting to the Warden.

warden_log|Three warehouse-opening orders use the name of an employee who left years ago. Their account is still accepted.|Can the Warden revoke it now?|Yes, but the warehouse must remain open for rescues. Identify the abused access so the whole station does not lose its supplies.|I will report the account that needs checking.|You can review the orders before reporting.|You retain the three orders identifying the old account.

warden_six|I will revoke the old account. Before you investigate the warehouse, I need to know you can bring your party home.|What does your test focus on?|Keeping a party able to fight when forced to switch. Access does not authorize destroying equipment or chasing people alone.|I am ready for the test.|Prepare your party and return. There is no need to issue access prematurely.|Then show me how you keep your party together under pressure.

warden_orders|Rocket rented the warehouse under a transport company's name. Duc works nights there. He can show you an entrance that will not alert the whole building.|What should I do first if I find Iris?|Get her to safety. Keep evidence if you can, but do not leave a person behind to bring back more equipment.|I will meet Duc before entering.|We will keep the records at the station while you prepare.|Meet Duc first. Bring Iris out before worrying about the machines.

rocket_informant|I hear Pokémon battles below the warehouse. The morning shift log says the basement is unused. Vex reads that log every day.|How can I find the way down?|The side door accepts the Black Card. The delivery board lists crates sent below. Read it before passing the checkpoints.|I will check the delivery board.|I have not led anyone downstairs. Prepare first.|Start with the board. It shows which corridor the deliveries use.

rocket_route|The copying machines are labeled fragile cargo. The basement has a separate power line and three checkpoints.|Will the Black Card open all three checkpoints?|No. It only gets you through the side door. Guards check people after that. The delivery record shows the route to Iris's room.|I will follow the route on the delivery record.|Read the route again before entering if you need to.|You retain the route and the locations of the three checkpoints.

rocket_guard1|The card is accepted. Its holder is not. My orders keep strangers outside this checkpoint.|Do you know someone is being held downstairs?|I know there is a restricted room. I cannot see its occupant list. Beat me if you want to pass.|I will battle to pass the checkpoint.|Stay outside, then. I do not chase people who have not entered.|Fine. This checkpoint opens if you win.

rocket_overhear|Vex: 'Keep the battle history. Delete the participants.' Iris: 'Bad data will make the system misidentify Pokémon.'|What does Vex want the records for?|Rocket forges access and sells it as valid cards. One repeatedly erased record starts with T. Iris is being forced to edit that data.|I will find the way to Iris's room.|You can listen again before moving on.|You retain the exchange as evidence and continue toward Iris.

rocket_guard2|The first checkpoint let you through? I have no orders to admit visitors to the machines.|Whose orders are you waiting for?|Vex's. Until then, I keep you here. My party does not need to finish quickly; it just needs to keep you away from the door.|I accept the battle. Let us see how long you can hold it.|If you stay back, I have no reason to start yet.|Then I will stop you at this checkpoint.

rocket_guard3|Past this door is an area absent from the visitor map. You have come too far to be lost.|Is Iris behind that door?|She works inside under Vex's supervision. I hold the door. Win if you want it opened.|I will battle to clear the way.|Step back and the battle has not begun.|All right. I am not stepping aside without a battle.

rocket_vex|The League erased these names before I found them. You demand answers from me; did you ask them the same questions?|Does their wrongdoing justify holding Iris?|No. I needed her to run the machine, and I kept her here. Beat me if you want to take her and the records out.|I will defeat you and bring Iris out.|Stop there if you are not ready to battle. I have not handed over access.|Then we settle who controls that door in this battle.

iris_rescue|I edited a report to keep our research group open. Rocket found the original and used it to force more work from me. I am not innocent.|What evidence did you preserve?|A separate reader contains an unedited copy. Take it, then we leave by the delivery door. I will explain what I did using the original.|I will take the original and bring you out.|I will keep the reader here. Do not erase the data yourself.|Take the reader's copy. I will follow you to the delivery door.

iris_terminal|The erased trainer is named TOBA. The original has signatures from Hale, Aurelia and someone at the School of Wolf.|Do those signatures identify who ordered the deletion?|Not yet. It does not give the reason. I will keep a copy; you keep the original. Marlow knows the archive system from before the current League.|I will bring the original to Marlow.|Keep this version intact if you want to examine it further.|You retain the original, including all three signatures.

marlow_account|The printed photo and digital record both omit a person. The old print still has an embossed mark the scan missed.|What can you read from that mark?|The Black Card was an old rescue credential, not Rocket's invention. The date beneath the photo may connect the erased record to that rescue.|I will examine the old photograph.|I will leave the print at the comparison table.|Start with the date below the photograph.

marlow_photo|TOBA stands beside Hale in the rescue team. Its date matches an incident the League records call an exercise.|Who can confirm what happened there?|The Seventh Warden keeps that area. He can grant access after a safety test. This photo gives you something specific to ask, not the whole answer.|I will take this lead to the Seventh Warden.|Compare the photos further if you need to.|You keep the photograph and incident date together.

warden_seven|I know part of the record was hidden. I also know the area is still dangerous. Pass my test before entering.|Who should I see about the rescue records afterward?|Liora at the eighth town's harbor kept the final ship's records. Bring the photo and date, not just a story you heard.|I am ready to battle for access.|I do not grant access before you are ready.|Then show me that your party can handle the journey.

liora_harbour|Show me the photograph and its date. Before opening the rescue list, I need to know which voyage you are comparing.|Is the original list still at the harbor?|Yes, on the operations board. The ship returned one person short. Read it first; Dorian will receive you for the final qualifier afterward.|I will compare the list on the board.|The harbor keeps the records. There is no need to rush.|Read the original beside the public version.

harbour_manifest|The original says TOBA did not board the returning ship. The public version says he did not join the rescue.|What does that change remove?|It erases that he went with the team at all. Liora cannot open the deeper record; the Battle Tower holds the final confirmation. Dorian's qualifier is the next step.|I will meet Dorian and continue comparing the records.|Keep both versions instead of treating them as equivalent.|You retain both versions of the passenger record.

dorian_qualifier|Liora sent your record. This is the final coastal round before the Battle Tower. My rain team is ready.|What does a rain team test?|Keeping your party effective when the weather changes, rather than relying on one Pokémon. Pass and you can enter the archive holding the final confirmation.|I accept. Let us begin.|Prepare first. I will keep your place in the qualifier.|Then we begin the final coastal round.

false_victory|You passed the final round. Congratulations. A new confirmation just arrived for your record, and something is wrong with it.|What is wrong with that confirmation?|It bears TOBA's signature, dated today. The missing person is being recorded as a results approver. The Battle Tower needs to explain it.|I will take the confirmation to the Tower.|Look at the signature again first. I kept an extra copy.|Take my copy too. Ask them how that signature was accepted.

tower_entry|Your qualifier record is valid. You face Rowan, Nyx, then Orion. Each holds a confirmation from the old system.|Can I read those confirmations now?|They belong to the trial records. Complete each battle in order to open the next copy. Your place is registered.|I will begin with Rowan.|Your place will remain registered when you return.|Rowan is first. We will record each round separately.

tower_rowan|My copy lists TOBA as the winner. The public version has no such battle. Pass my trial to examine the full copy.|How is your trial different from the qualifier?|I watch how you prepare for the next turn. A good move leaves your party room to respond when the opponent changes plans.|I am ready to battle.|The record is staying here. Prepare first.|Then let us see how you prepare for the turn after this one.

tower_nyx|My copy awards all points for TOBA's battle. The League calls it cancelled. After my tempo trial, you can compare them.|What should I watch about the tempo?|Do not attack only because your turn arrived. My party can change action order. Notice when waiting gives you an advantage.|I accept your trial.|I am not timing your preparation.|All right. The tempo trial begins with this battle.

tower_orion|Aurelia ordered the record kept private. The public version made that a deletion. Distinguish those two decisions.|Do you know who changed the order?|Not enough evidence to name someone. Pass this trial and you may take the order to Aurelia herself.|I will battle to open the next record.|Keep that question. Taking time to prepare does not make it less valid.|Then earn access to the order itself.

league_entry|Aurelia received your request. The records will be preserved, including the parts this office needs to explain.|Who do I meet before Aurelia?|Cassian, Seraph and Kael, in order. Each kept a separate account of the old experiment. After those battles, the Champion will receive you.|I will start with Cassian.|Your request remains on record.|Your first appointment is with Cassian.

elite_cassian|I helped preserve TOBA's result. The battle remained, but his name disappeared from its participant list.|Why preserve a result while erasing its participant?|The rescue system needed the result to keep running. When we could not establish whether TOBA lived, we allowed his name to be erased. You receive my record after this battle.|I accept your battle.|I will still owe you that answer when you return.|Then let us battle. Afterward I will give you my record.

elite_seraph|I wrote some of these papers. A sentence can be accurate in every word and still hide exactly what the reader needs.|Did you turn the privacy order into a deletion order?|The office changed it. I bear responsibility for its route, but cannot prove Aurelia did not know. After this battle you receive my comparison.|I will battle and keep that comparison.|Pausing does not mean abandoning your question.|Then we battle. Keep the comparison with the original order afterward.

elite_kael|I left the test room with the group. TOBA stayed to keep the Pokémon alive. Those who returned cannot speak in his place.|Did you know he was still inside when you withdrew?|Yes. Vargan opposed closing the archive; Aurelia chose secrecy. I said too little about knowing he remained. After this battle I will sign my account.|I accept. Afterward I want your full account.|I will keep that promise even if you need more time.|Then we begin. My account will carry my own name.

champion_aurelia|I heard from Hale, Mara and Iris. You brought enough evidence that another promise to answer later is no longer acceptable.|Will you answer about TOBA after this battle?|Yes. I will name what I knew and what I decided. First, complete the Champion battle.|I am ready to face you.|Prepare if you need to. Your record will not be closed.|Then we begin the Champion battle.

aurelia_aftermath|I ordered secrecy to prevent the experiment being repeated. When secrecy became deletion, I knew. I let it continue.|What does Vargan keep that you have not shown me?|The original at the School of Wolf. I chose silence over admitting someone was left behind. You may read it and question Vargan. I must disclose my part.|I will read the original at the School.|Your access remains, even if you do not leave immediately.|Take the authorization. I will begin my own public account.

wolf_bran|Your introduction is valid. Before entering the archive, pass the School's rescue trials. I will explain the order.|What are those trials?|Fen tests discipline, Skoll observation, and Hati rescue preparation. Supplies go to the station; they are not an entrance fee.|I will begin with Fen.|I will keep your introduction until you are ready.|Fen is first. Ask if any instruction is unclear.

wolf_fen|Keeping a party alive during a rescue means knowing when to stop attacking. We begin with a battle.|What should I do after it?|Read Skoll's trail marks before the next trial. Observing the route and the battle are both part of preparation.|I am ready for your trial.|Prepare your party. I do not begin before you accept.|Then show me how you keep your party able to respond.

wolf_track|Human footprints turn back. Pokémon tracks continue. The rescue group lost contact here.|Does this prove someone chose to stay behind?|No. It only shows the group turned back after replies stopped. Skoll wants you to distinguish observation from inference.|I will take that observation to Skoll.|You can inspect the trail further before answering.|You retain the trail directions without assuming a motive.

wolf_skoll|You read the trail. Now I want to see you observe an opponent without time to pause.|Which signs should I watch?|Switches, moves already used, and which Pokémon the opponent is trying to preserve. I change tempo. You need to remember what you saw, not guess.|I am ready to battle.|Observing your own party is useful preparation too.|Then we begin. Keep track of what changes.

wolf_supply|The station needs supplies for its next rescue. Understand that preparation before taking the next battle trial.|Will these supplies actually be used?|Yes. They enter the rescue stock and are not returned after this conversation. Check the Phone's list and deliver only when you have enough.|I will hand over the listed supplies.|Return if you do not have enough. Do not take another team's supplies.|I will count the supplies against the list before accepting them.

wolf_hati|The supplies are recorded. Next is keeping your party effective while moving quickly. Want to begin?|How is this different from Skoll's trial?|I apply pressure with speed. Choose what matters first rather than solving everything in one turn. Afterward you meet Vargan.|I accept. Let us begin.|Your supplies remain recorded. You will not deliver them again.|Then the speed trial begins. The supply delivery is already recorded.

wolf_vargan|I reviewed all three trials. The archive is behind this door. One battle with me remains before you enter.|Does winning let me read all of the originals?|Yes. Three records are stored separately. Read all three. I will not decide which part you may know.|I am ready to battle you.|The door will still be here. Prepare your party first.|Then we battle. If you win, all three records are available.

archive_record1|TOBA entered the test room voluntarily to rescue trapped Pokémon. There is no order forcing him to enter.|What did Hale promise before TOBA went in?|I promise to keep the way back open. The record stops when the system loses contact. The other two records cover what followed.|I will read the second record.|You can review that promise before continuing.|You retain the promise and its timestamp before reading on.

archive_record2|This record preserves two finish times for the final battle. The public copy keeps one, like the anomaly at the training grounds.|Did TOBA still send commands after the others withdrew?|Yes. Rescue commands continued. Nobody verified he was alive; the record does not prove he died either.|I will read the final archive order.|Keep both times for the next comparison.|You retain both timestamps and the later rescue commands.

archive_record3|Aurelia ordered secrecy. The office changed it to deletion. Vargan kept the original. Hale received the edited copy and said nothing.|What should I ask Hale about this?|Why he accepted the edit without checking the way back he promised TOBA. These papers record several people's decisions, not a single culprit.|I will ask Hale about this record.|Compare all three records again before asking if you need to.|You retain the chain of decisions for Hale to answer.

archive_hale|I thought one more day would give us a certain answer. Then I waited another. Eventually I lived as though nobody could ask me to keep that promise.|Will you help us find TOBA now?|Yes. I will call Mara, Aurelia and Orin and reopen the comparison. If the sender is TOBA, we need to hear him together. You should not face this alone.|I will stay in contact and go with the group.|I will still prepare my part. I will not send you in my place again.|All right. I will contact the others and keep the line open.

final_unknown|The sender called the station: I know you have read the records. I want you to hear the rest from me.|Has the group checked who sent it?|Orin confirmed the signature matches. Mara keeps contact; Aurelia knows. The meeting is saved on your Phone. Nobody has yet identified the person there.|I will go to the meeting and stay in contact.|Prepare first. Contact with the sender has not been lost.|Take the saved meeting point and keep the group informed.

final_confrontation|You kept the original. I helped you, hid some things, and asked you to open doors I could not open myself.|Are you TOBA?|After this battle I will answer with my name. I want both participants kept in the result, without another altered confirmation.|I accept, with the original record preserved.|I will not change your copy. Prepare your party and return.|Then we begin with both participants recorded.

final_explanation|My name is TOBA. The Pokémon brought me through a side rescue exit. I lived, but the system treated every request to return as forged.|Why did you also use Rocket to reopen the system?|I kept an old copy and inserted confirmations when access opened. Rocket wanted to sell access; I used them to open a route. I used you too. I will not call that innocent.|I will bring your account back to the group.|Compare my account with the original before believing it.|Take my account, and check it against the records you kept.

final_choice|We will restore TOBA's name, preserve the Rocket evidence, and disclose the old order. We cannot ask you to treat that as resolving everything.|Who will sign the testimony and preserve the records?|Iris testifies. Rook hands over copies; Vargan opens the archive to investigators. I answer for my order. TOBA should not have to prove his existence again.|I agree to preserve the testimony in the public record.|Review it if you are not ready to confirm. We must still do what we promised.|Your testimony will remain with the originals. We will record who is responsible for each step.

epilogue_hale|TOBA sent a message. He signed his full name. As for you, are you coming home for dinner?|What will everyone do after the investigation?|Iris needs a new place to work. Orin is comparing reports, and Mara wants more practice. I would like us to meet when nothing urgent is happening too.|I will come for dinner. You should take a break as well.|Come when you can. I will not turn dinner into a meeting.|Then I will put the work away before dinner. Hold me to that.

epilogue_mara|I rearranged my party. The next battle can wait, though. You just finished a long journey.|We will still have a rematch, right?|Yes. Pick a day and message me. Hale is waiting for dinner today. I do not want to miss another appointment either.|I will message you to arrange the next battle.|Rest first. My party is not going anywhere.|Agreed. We arrange the battle later; today we keep the dinner appointment.
